_comment: Guided tour for the docking card. Steps point at real controls; the ones with an await wait until the user presses the control.

steps.title: What this tool does
steps.text:
FRET distances between dyes tell you how two or more rigid structures sit relative to each other. This tool moves the bodies until the distances the labels should give (from their accessible volumes) match the ones you measured, and scores how well they do.

You need the structures and an fps.json file that holds the labelling positions and the measured distances. Seven steps; you press the buttons, the tour only points at them.

steps.title: Load the example, or a project
steps.text: Load example copies the shipped HIV reverse transcriptase project (the protein, its DNA and an fps.json with 20 measured distances) into your settings folder and fills every input. Project loads a docking project of your own: the structures, the fps.json and the parameters in one file. Or add the pieces yourself in the next steps.

steps.title: The rigid bodies
steps.text: One structure per rigid body, in the order of their body ids. Add Files adds one (so does dropping a .pdb on the window). The same file twice is a homodimer.

steps.title: The restraints
steps.text: fps.json chooses the labelling and distance file. Build one in ChiMOL's labelling editor (Tools › Labelling).

steps.title: Choose what to do
steps.text: Op selects dock (rigid-body docking), refine, screen (rank a library of structures) or score (one structure). Runs above 1 repeats the docking from random starts to estimate how well the distances determine the result.

steps.title: Run it
steps.text: Press Run. The bar shows the progress and the best score so far; Stop ends the run.

steps.title: Read the result
steps.text: Each result is a row of the Results table (best score first); select one to see its structure in the Structure tab and the Score tab for the trace. Press Help for the scores and the files written.
